reviewer_summary.question: Why must a chosen word be processed before choosing the following word, and how do separate stores at each layer save work?
reviewer_summary.takeaway: Choosing blue uses the previous word’s finished number; processing blue makes its own number while reusing earlier keys and values that later text cannot change.

findings.problem: The complete calculation starts before explaining why The’s result helps reach the next choice.

resolution.note: Show the destination is-finished-number-to-next-choice first, then motivate learning the reading rule from the smallest earlier source.

findings.problem: Three silent products advance too quickly under general narration.

resolution.note: Name each source’s computed product, scan source rows calmly, and extend the batch pause.

findings.problem: Three silent fraction results must be retained through the following value reminders.

resolution.note: Name each source’s fraction, extend the pause, and retain computed fractions visibly during value reminders.

findings.problem: Temporary numbers obscure the target actual fractions.

resolution.note: Keep a stable calculate-parts-then-divide-by-total guide through the intermediate arithmetic.

findings.problem: The new signed multiplication case leaves the self product entirely to silent inspection.

resolution.note: Speak every named match result, including blue’s positive self product; all actual multiplications remain on screen.

findings.problem: Eight expanded key/value pairs compete with the old/new distinction.

resolution.note: Expand only The’s pair at both layers, keep other K/V entries compact, and explicitly label blue new versus earlier entries old.
